QF.id: XXVA Regulatory Compliance for Non-Core Research Personnel_15

question.text: The Exchange surveillance mechanisms GSM (Graded Surveillance Measure) and ASM (Additional Surveillance Measure) are relevant for research services because:

answer.text: They provide guaranteed buy signals for stocks under surveillance

Stocks under GSM / ASM can face safeguards such as trade-for-trade settlement, surveillance deposits, reduced price bands, increased margins, price freezes, and ASM margin escalation, which may affect the implementability and risk profile of research recommendations
They are only relevant for stock exchanges and have no impact on research activities
They automatically disqualify stocks from being covered in research reports

explanation.text: The Logic: GSM and ASM can subject securities to safeguards such as trade-for-trade settlement, surveillance deposits, reduced price bands, increased margins, price freezes, and ASM margin escalation. These safeguards directly affect how investors can act on a research recommendation and therefore matter for both the analyst and the sales / distribution function. The Trap: GSM / ASM neither act as buy signals, nor are they irrelevant to research, nor do they automatically disqualify a security from research coverage; they change the conditions under which the security can be traded. Note: Surveillance status changes over time, so it is worth checking exchange notifications before circulating a recommendation on names that have recently appeared in the GSM / ASM lists.
